acceptance_criteria.criterion: A "Polling discipline" subsection exists in the Monitoring Progress section of the persona source
The subsection specifies a minimum polling interval of 30 seconds
The subsection specifies a 60-second backoff when JSONL line count is unchanged
The subsection limits consecutive empty get_terminal_output checks to 3 before switching to JSONL
The subsection caps total polling iterations at 10 before pausing and informing the user
node scripts/build-personas.js --check passes after the change

summary: Added a 'Polling discipline' subsection to personas/standalone/src/content/orchestrator-runner.md, inserted after the line-pattern table in the 'Live terminal output' subsection and before 'JSONL log file'. The subsection specifies: 30-second minimum polling interval, 3 consecutive empty get_terminal_output checks before switching to JSONL, 60-second JSONL backoff when line count is unchanged, and a 10-iteration total cap with user notification. Rebuilt both ledger and standalone persona suites; all builds pass. node scripts/build-personas.js --check confirmed up-to-date for ledger suite.

comments.note: No observations — code in the touched files is clean and consistent. The persona content follows established style; the new subsection fits naturally into the Monitoring Progress structure alongside the existing Live terminal output and JSONL log file subsections.

summary: PASS with Fix-Forward. The 'Polling discipline' subsection is clear, actionable, and correctly scoped. All four rules (30-second interval, 3-check empty limit, 60-second JSONL backoff, 10-iteration cap with user notification) are unambiguous and free of conflicts with surrounding guidance. Applied one Fix-Forward: the intro sentence 'Terminal output from `get_terminal_output` is free to read, but repeated polling in a tight loop wastes tokens on empty responses' was mildly contradictory (the section heading says 'zero extra cost' while warning about token waste). Replaced with 'Calling `get_terminal_output` to check progress is convenient, but polling in a tight loop wastes tokens on empty responses.' Fix applied to source and both generated targets; `node scripts/build-personas.js --suite standalone` confirms clean rebuild.

comments.note: Fix-Forward applied: replaced 'Terminal output from `get_terminal_output` is free to read' with 'Calling `get_terminal_output` to check progress is convenient' in `personas/standalone/src/content/orchestrator-runner.md` and both generated targets. The original phrasing was internally inconsistent — 'free to read' implies zero cost, but the sentence immediately warns about token waste. The revised wording removes the ambiguity without changing any rule or behavior.

notes: Polling discipline subsection added and both persona targets rebuilt. The Reviewer should verify the new rules are clear, actionable, and correctly scoped — specifically that the 3-check terminal limit, 60-second JSONL backoff, and 10-iteration cap are unambiguous and do not conflict with any other guidance in the persona (e.g. the Monitoring Progress introduction or Common Errors table).
